marks.gloss_en: and the Sages forbid [it] -- the words of R' Yehuda
wool dangling on a firstborn: what appears with the shearing is permitted

מתיב רב ששת: ... ורבי יוסי אומר יבקר -- with the baraita construed of a blemished firstborn's shearings (25b.8), יבוקר means whether the blemish is permanent or passing, אף על גב שלא התירו מומחה (25b.9): R' Yosei permits without an expert
blemished ones [mixed in] forbid in any amount
לא; יבוקר -- אי התירו מומחה אין, ואי לא לא (= p_rava_yevukar_hitiro)
Rava: no -- 'let it be examined' whether an expert permitted it: if so, yes; if not, no
מיתיבי: התולש צמר מבכור תם ... אסור; טעמא דתם, הא בעל מום שרי, אף על פי שלא התירו מומחה!
one who plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn, even though it then developed a blemish and he slaughtered it -- forbidden
(entertained) by implication of R' Yosei's 'not in this', Akavya forbids [the wool] where the animal was slaughtered
where he slaughtered it, all agree [the wool] is permitted; they dispute where it died
the dispute is where an expert permitted [the animal]
(entertained) 'let it be examined' means: [find] the blemished one and remove it
here we deal with the shearings of a blemished firstborn mixed with ordinary shearings
Rav Sheshet: 'let it be examined' -- is it not whether it is a permanent or a passing blemish, even though no expert permitted it?
R' Chiyya bar Abba's R' Yochanan: the dispute is where he examined and did not find
and they dispute as R' Meir and the Rabbis dispute
and the Sages say: he digs until he reaches rock or virgin soil
R' Asi's R' Yochanan: the dispute is where he examined and found
a field in which a grave was lost: one who enters it is impure
R' Asi's ground: impurity may have been carried off by a raven or a mouse; but a blemished animal -- where would it go?
R' Chiyya bar Abba's ground: a field is a usual burial place, so another may have been buried; but consecrated animals, once examined and whole -- is it their way to develop a blemish?
